children: Risk management principles point to raising interest rates as insurance against persistently elevated inflation, said Claudia Sahm, founder of Sahm Consulting and former Federal Reserve and White House economist.
Markets currently put the odds of a rate increase at less than 20%, but "the case for a rate hike is stronger than the odds suggest," Sahm wrote.
She noted that risk management was the most common reason given in the FOMC minutes for the September rate increase, calling it "a signature approach of the Powell Fed."

Sahm's confidence in disinflation has shifted dramatically over the course of the year, she explained. Early in the year, she believed the temporary boost from energy prices and tariffs would wane, delivering necessary disinflation.
"By the end of the summer, I was much less confident," she said, adding that by September she "shifted to favoring modest rate hikes as insurance against persistently elevated inflation."
The economist emphasized that long lags between changes in the policy rate and their effects on inflation argue for adjusting policy sooner rather than later.

Recent inflation data has only reinforced her concerns, according to Sahm. The September CPI "offered little to build confidence in disinflation," with the upside surprise being broad-based rather than concentrated in a single category, and the core CPI rising at an annualized rate of about 4%.
The September PPI showed "even more pricing pressure in the pipeline," with transportation and warehousing costs "increasing at a pace last seen in 2022."
Energy prices continue to climb, and she noted the pass-through to food, airfares, and other core prices "builds for months after the shock."

Fed officials remain divided on timing, Sahm observed. Fed Governor Bowman has argued that under uncertainty, "it is best to move slowly and see how the economy responds before raising rates again," while Cleveland Fed President Hammack has made the opposite case for "small adjustments relatively quickly."
With the Fed's vote coming less than a week before the midterm elections, Sahm stressed that "the Fed must ignore that fact" and ground its decision in economics, not politics.
"If it moves away from that, even to delay until after the election, it weakens its claim to independence," she said.

title: Interest rates should be raised as insurance against persistent inflation – economist
